note_en: Legal Chinese uses 不得 (bùdé) for "must not / may not" and 应当 (yīngdāng) for "shall": 试用期内员工的工资不得低于当地最低工资标准 "wages during probation may not be lower than the local minimum wage." In everyday speech you'd say 不能 and 应该, but in laws and contracts 不得 and 应当 sound as formal as English "shall not" and "shall."
